variant_decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'And there was set food before him to eat', a passive with no expressed agent, which matches the qere hophal wa-yusam. But the ketiv is written without vowels and its consonants carry no voice distinction: the same letters can be pointed as a passive, so the English passive does not exclude it. No ASV note is mapped to this verse, and nothing else in GEN.24.33 turns on the choice. Both readings remain compatible; the qere base fallback carries the projection.

review_notes: Corrected the placement of the ASV's 'that'. The accepted alignment gave it to the presentative wayhî and marked the apodosis waw unrepresented, on the ground that 'no apodosis waw is written for the ASV's that'; but a waw does open the apodosis (s011, וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ), which is exactly rule 45's second case, where the waw carries the 'that' and the verb keeps only 'it came to pass'.

The ASV prints 'that' before the temporal clause ('came to pass, that, when ... heard'), so the corrected unit is reordered relative to the Hebrew; rule 25 allows this, and rule 45 offers position as a consequence rather than as the deciding evidence.

The chapter's other three presentative frames — 24.15, 24.22, 24.30 — all place the 'that' on the apodosis waw, so the corrected reading also matches how the same construction was resolved elsewhere in GEN.24.
